newsitem.title: FRANCE: French welfare bill sets 1997 spending target.
newsitem.headline: French welfare bill sets 1997 spending target.

text.p: France's Labour and Social Affairs Ministry said on Wednesday that its social security spending target for 1997 was 600.2 billion francs, a 10 billion franc increase from 1996.
In a statement, the ministry said that in recent years, spending has risen by over 30 billion francs a year.
The statement said a lot of progress had been made toward reining in welfare spending and that the rate of increase in social security benefits paid out in 1996 should be 1.7 percent.
In 1990 the rate of increase was four 4.0 percent, the statement said. It added that the rate should drop below 1.0 percent in 1997.
The statement, repeating earlier statements by the government's spokesman, said the welfare deficit would be cut to 29.7 billion francs in 1997 from 51.5 billion francs in 1996.

"One percent of spending growth in volume is more rigourous than would be needed if the system were not in deficit, but is absolutely necessary in the existing circumstances to accelerate the sustainable return to balance of the accounts," the statement said.
